titulo_es: Los mejores momentos de la historia
estandares: Narro hechos pasados en secuencia usando verbos regulares e irregulares. Comprendo textos cortos sobre acontecimientos históricos y culturales.
competencias: Usar el pasado simple en sus tres formas; distinguir verbos regulares e irregulares; preguntar por hechos pasados con question words; hablar de fechas, lugares de la ciudad y géneros de cine.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En parejas, los estudiantes eligen un acontecimiento histórico o una película basada en hechos reales y presentan una línea de tiempo narrada en pasado simple, con al menos cinco verbos irregulares.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In pairs, students choose a historical event or a film based on real events and present a timeline narrated in the simple past, using at least five irregular verbs.

lecciones.t: Pasado simple: afirmativo, negativo e interrogativo
lecciones.t_en: Simple past: affirmative, negative and interrogative
lecciones.content_es:
Para qué sirve

Habla de acciones terminadas en un momento concreto del pasado: I watched a movie yesterday.

Las tres formas

  • Afirmativo: verbo en pasado — She played tennis.
  • Negativo: didn't + verbo base — She didn't play tennis.
  • Pregunta: Did + sujeto + verbo base — Did she play tennis?

La regla de oro

El pasado se marca una sola vez. Si aparece did o didn't, el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base: Did you went? es incorrecto; lo correcto es Did you go?

Respuestas cortas: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
lecciones.content_en:
What it is for

It talks about finished actions at a specific moment in the past: I watched a movie yesterday.

The three forms

  • Affirmative: past verb — She played tennis.
  • Negative: didn't + base verb — She didn't play tennis.
  • Question: Did + subject + base verb — Did she play tennis?

The golden rule

The past is marked only once. If did or didn't appears, the main verb goes back to its base form: Did you went? is wrong; the correct form is Did you go?

Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

fichas.d: El pasado ya está en didn't: I didn't go, no didn't went.
fichas.d_en: The past is already in didn't: I didn't go, not didn't went.

fichas.d_en: Word order of the simple past question.

fichas.d: O el verbo o el auxiliar, nunca los dos.

quiz.why_en: With did the main verb goes in base form: see.

quiz.why: Didn't ya marca el pasado, así que el verbo queda en base.
quiz.why_en: Didn't already marks the past, so the verb stays in base form.

quiz.q_en: Short answer to "Did she call you?" (yes)

quiz.why_en: The short answer repeats the auxiliary did.

lecciones.content_es:
La terminación -ed

Los verbos regulares forman el pasado agregando -ed: work → worked, play → played.

Reglas de escritura

  • Termina en -e → solo -d: like → liked
  • Consonante + y → -ied: study → studied, cry → cried
  • Vocal + y → -ed: play → played
  • Consonante-vocal-consonante corta → se dobla: stop → stopped, plan → planned

Las tres pronunciaciones de -ed

  • /t/ después de sonido sordo: worked, watched, stopped
  • /d/ después de sonido sonoro: played, lived, cleaned
  • /ɪd/ después de t o d: wanted, needed, visited
lecciones.content_en:
The -ed ending

Regular verbs form the past by adding -ed: work → worked, play → played.

Spelling rules

  • Ends in -e → just -d: like → liked
  • Consonant + y → -ied: study → studied, cry → cried
  • Vowel + y → -ed: play → played
  • Short consonant-vowel-consonant → double it: stop → stopped, plan → planned

The three pronunciations of -ed

  • /t/ after a voiceless sound: worked, watched, stopped
  • /d/ after a voiced sound: played, lived, cleaned
  • /ɪd/ after t or d: wanted, needed, visited

fichas.d: Consonante + y se convierte en -ied.
fichas.d_en: Consonant + y becomes -ied.

fichas.d: Se dobla la consonante final en verbos cortos.
fichas.d_en: The final consonant doubles in short verbs.

fichas.d: Los verbos que terminan en t o d suman una sílaba.
fichas.d_en: Verbs ending in t or d add an extra syllable.

fichas.d: Si ya termina en -e, solo se agrega -d.
fichas.d_en: If it already ends in -e, just add -d.

quiz.why_en: Consonant + y changes to -ied.

quiz.why: Se dobla la p por ser consonante-vocal-consonante corta.
quiz.why_en: The p doubles because it is a short consonant-vowel-consonant verb.

quiz.why: Visit termina en t, así que -ed suma una sílaba.
quiz.why_en: Visit ends in t, so -ed adds an extra syllable.

lecciones.content_es:
No siguen la regla

Estos verbos cambian de forma y hay que aprenderlos de memoria. Son los más usados del idioma.

Los más frecuentes

  • go → went · come → came · see → saw
  • do → did · make → made · take → took
  • get → got · give → gave · have → had
  • say → said · tell → told · think → thought
  • write → wrote · read → read (se escribe igual, suena /red/)
  • eat → ate · drink → drank · buy → bought

Recuerda

La forma irregular solo aparece en afirmativo. En negativo y pregunta vuelve la forma base: I went → I didn't go → Did you go?
lecciones.content_en:
They do not follow the rule

These verbs change their form and must be learned by heart. They are the most used ones in the language.

The most frequent

  • go → went · come → came · see → saw
  • do → did · make → made · take → took
  • get → got · give → gave · have → had
  • say → said · tell → told · think → thought
  • write → wrote · read → read (same spelling, pronounced /red/)
  • eat → ate · drink → drank · buy → bought

Remember

The irregular form only appears in the affirmative. In negatives and questions the base form comes back: I went → I didn't go → Did you go?

fichas.d: Uno de los irregulares más usados.
fichas.d_en: One of the most used irregular verbs.

fichas.d: No confundir con say → said.
fichas.d_en: Not to be confused with say → said.

fichas.d_en: The -ought group: buy, think, bring.

fichas.d: Con did/didn't el verbo vuelve a la forma base.
fichas.d_en: With did/didn't the verb returns to its base form.

quiz.why_en: See is irregular: its simple past is saw.

quiz.why_en: The simple past of eat is ate.

quiz.why_en: After didn't the irregular verb returns to its base form.

lecciones.t_en: Question words with the simple past
lecciones.content_es:
La estructura

Wh- + did + sujeto + verbo base:

  • Where did you go last summer?
  • What did she say?
  • When did the war start?
  • Why did they leave?
  • How did he learn English?

Cuando el Wh- es el sujeto

Si preguntas quién o qué hizo la acción, no se usa did y el verbo va en pasado:

  • Who wrote this book? (no Who did write)
  • What happened yesterday?

How much / How many

How many people came? · How much did it cost?
lecciones.content_en:
The structure

Wh- + did + subject + base verb:

  • Where did you go last summer?
  • What did she say?
  • When did the war start?
  • Why did they leave?
  • How did he learn English?

When the Wh- word is the subject

If you ask who or what did the action, did is not used and the verb goes in the past:

  • Who wrote this book? (not Who did write)
  • What happened yesterday?

How much / How many

How many people came? · How much did it cost?

fichas.d_en: Fixed word order for past questions.

fichas.d: Si Who es el sujeto, el verbo va en pasado sin did.
fichas.d_en: If Who is the subject, the verb goes in the past with no did.

fichas.d: Pregunta por el hecho: no lleva did.
fichas.d_en: Asks about the event itself: it takes no did.

fichas.d_en: Asking about a past price.

quiz.why_en: With did + subject the question asks for place, time or manner: Where.

quiz.why: Who es el sujeto: el verbo va en pasado y no lleva did.
quiz.why_en: Who is the subject: the verb goes in the past with no did.

quiz.why: Last weekend indica pasado: el auxiliar es did.
quiz.why_en: Last weekend signals the past: the auxiliary is did.

lecciones.content_es:
Escribir la fecha

Formato americano: March 15, 2026 (mes, día, año).
Formato británico: 15 March 2026.
Se lee con ordinal: March the fifteenth.

Los años

  • 1999 → nineteen ninety-nine
  • 2005 → two thousand five
  • 2026 → twenty twenty-six

Siglos y décadas

the 19th century (siglo XIX), the 1990s (los noventa).

Preposiciones

  • in + año, mes, siglo: in 1810, in July, in the 20th century
  • on + día o fecha exacta: on Monday, on July 20th
  • at + hora: at 7 o'clock
lecciones.content_en:
Writing the date

American format: March 15, 2026 (month, day, year).
British format: 15 March 2026.
It is read with an ordinal: March the fifteenth.

Years

  • 1999 → nineteen ninety-nine
  • 2005 → two thousand five
  • 2026 → twenty twenty-six

Centuries and decades

the 19th century, the 1990s.

Prepositions

  • in + year, month, century: in 1810, in July, in the 20th century
  • on + day or exact date: on Monday, on July 20th
  • at + time: at 7 o'clock

fichas.d: in año o mes, on día o fecha, at hora.
fichas.d_en: in for year or month, on for day or date, at for time.

fichas.d_en: The date is read with an ordinal number.

quiz.why_en: Exact dates take on.

quiz.why_en: Century with an ordinal indicates the century.

lecciones.content_es:
Lugares

library (biblioteca), bookstore (librería), museum, park, hospital, bank, post office (oficina de correos), police station, bus station, train station, market, mall (centro comercial), bakery (panadería), drugstore / pharmacy, church, square (plaza), stadium.

Falsos amigos

library NO es librería (esa es bookstore). drugstore es farmacia, no droguería de drogas ilegales.

Dar indicaciones

Go straight ahead. Turn left / right at the corner. It's on the right, next to the bank. Cross the street.
lecciones.content_en:
Places

library, bookstore, museum, park, hospital, bank, post office, police station, bus station, train station, market, mall, bakery, drugstore / pharmacy, church, square, stadium.

False friends

library is where you borrow books; a shop that sells them is a bookstore.

Giving directions

Go straight ahead. Turn left / right at the corner. It's on the right, next to the bank. Cross the street.

fichas.d_en: A library lends books; a bookstore sells them.

fichas.d_en: The place where you send letters.

fichas.d_en: To change direction at a corner.

fichas.d_en: Keep going without turning.

quiz.why_en: Cross the street means to go to the other side.

lecciones.content_es:
Géneros

action, comedy, drama, horror (terror), science fiction / sci-fi, romance, thriller (suspenso), animated movie, documentary, historical movie, adventure, musical.

Hablar de películas

  • What kind of movies do you like?
  • I watched a great documentary last night.
  • It was about the Second World War.
  • The ending was surprising.

Adjetivos de opinión

exciting, boring, scary, funny, touching (conmovedora), predictable.

Ojo: watch a movie, see a movie, pero go to the movies.
lecciones.content_en:
Genres

action, comedy, drama, horror, science fiction / sci-fi, romance, thriller, animated movie, documentary, historical movie, adventure, musical.

Talking about films

  • What kind of movies do you like?
  • I watched a great documentary last night.
  • It was about the Second World War.
  • The ending was surprising.

Opinion adjectives

exciting, boring, scary, funny, touching, predictable.

Careful: you watch or see a movie, but you go to the movies.

fichas.d_en: Structure used to tell what a film is about.

repaso.titulo: Repaso — The Best Moments in History!
repaso.titulo_en: Review — The Best Moments in History!
repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Todo el periodo es pasado simple. Los verbos regulares agregan -ed; los irregulares cambian de forma y hay que memorizarlos. En negativo y pregunta entra did y el verbo vuelve a su forma base.

Puntos gramaticales

  • Reglas de -ed: -d, -ied, doble consonante. Tres pronunciaciones: /t/, /d/, /ɪd/.
  • Irregulares frecuentes: go-went, see-saw, eat-ate, buy-bought, write-wrote.
  • Wh- + did + sujeto + verbo base; si el Wh- es el sujeto, no lleva did.

Vocabulario

Fechas, años y siglos con in / on / at; lugares de la ciudad e indicaciones; géneros de cine y adjetivos de opinión.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The whole term is the simple past. Regular verbs add -ed; irregular verbs change form and must be memorized. In negatives and questions did appears and the verb returns to its base form.

Grammar points

  • -ed rules: -d, -ied, doubled consonant. Three pronunciations: /t/, /d/, /ɪd/.
  • Frequent irregulars: go-went, see-saw, eat-ate, buy-bought, write-wrote.
  • Wh- + did + subject + base verb; if the Wh- word is the subject, no did.

Vocabulary

Dates, years and centuries with in / on / at; places around town and directions; film genres and opinion adjectives.
